review_status: draft v1 - pelagic offshore migratory profile

profile.size: Common up to 30 lb; Florida record 45 lb
profile.diet: Small fish, squids, crabs, and stomatopods
profile.behavior: Pelagic schooling fish that feeds heavily along thermal breaks, current edges, and seamounds/humps.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, ideal for active feeding blackfin tuna.
factors.value_notes: A northern Gulf satellite-tag study of nine blackfin tuna found 89% of recorded time at 21.9–26.6 °C (tagged fish ranged 13.9–32.9 °C). ICCAT summarizes a lower distribution limit near 20 °C. This supports the configured 20–29 °C / 22–27 °C band as broad species-level context, but the tag sample was small and geographically limited.

factors.reason_template: Temperature break strength is {per10km} C per 10 km; this is a provisional water-mass boundary proxy, not a validated blackfin preference.
factors.value_notes: Blackfin distribution is associated with upwelling, runoff, plankton concentrations, and water clarity, but these sources do not calibrate a preferred SST-gradient magnitude or validate a higher-is-better response. Retain as a provisional frontal-edge proxy.

factors.reason_template: A chlorophyll edge may indicate a productivity boundary; its value as a blackfin feeding predictor remains provisional.
factors.value_notes: Published summaries link blackfin distribution to plankton concentrations and upwelling/runoff, but do not establish remotely sensed chlorophyll-gradient strength as a direct feeding predictor. Retain as a provisional proxy.

factors.reason_template: Seafloor drops steeply ({value} m/km), marking humps and ledges blackfin tuna patrol.
factors.value_notes: A species synthesis links blackfin distribution to continental-shelf steepness and reports Florida occurrences along the shelf-slope edge. This supports a broad association with shelf-edge topography, but does not validate the runtime bottom_slope metric or a monotonic higher-is-better response.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in deep blue offshore waters.
factors.value_notes: Satellite tags recorded fish vertical depths of 0–217 m, with 90% of time at 0–57 m; fisheries syntheses describe adults near the shelf-slope edge and generally at less than about 183 m bottom depth. Fish vertical dive depth is not identical to seafloor bathymetry. The configured 30–1,500 m / 60–800 m bathymetric band is only partly supported and likely broader than observed common habitat. Depth is an active gate.

factors.reason_template: The inshore Gulf Stream edge is {abs_value} km {side}; this is a provisional proximity indicator, not a validated blackfin distance preference.
factors.value_notes: Sources describe blackfin as a warm-water pelagic tuna associated with shelf-slope edges and oceanographic features, but do not establish a preferred distance from the Gulf Stream edge or validate the configured distance band. Keep as a provisional geographic proxy.

text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.night: It is night, when nocturnal feeding is high.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
